headline: Forest are 19th, yet the market still makes them favourites
summary: Nottingham Forest are 19th in the Premier League with 5 points from 7 games and three straight defeats, yet they go to Ipswich on Friday as the favourites. According to Yahoo Sports, Morgan Gibbs-White is fit to return, and Forest's 1.72 expected goals a game show a side still creating chances. Ipswich led at Manchester City on Saturday before losing 3-2, and they lose Sasa Lukic again — 502 minutes in midfield this season. Across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Forest are 42.5% to win; the handicap rates them only about a quarter of a goal better. The goals line sits at 2.7, a game just under three goals.
read: Nottingham Forest are 19th with 5 points from 7 and arrive at Ipswich having lost three straight, yet the market still makes them 42.5% favourites — consistent with their 1.72 xG per game and the return of Morgan Gibbs-White. Ipswich sit 10th, score regularly (9 goals in 5), but lose Sasa Lukic again in midfield; the goals line of 2.7 points to an open, close game.

facts.fact: Nottingham Forest are 19th in the Premier League with 5 points from 7 games, on a run of three straight defeats.
facts.meaning: A side in the bottom three travelling to a mid-table team, with early scrutiny on the new head coach.

facts.fact: Gary O'Neil has confirmed Sasa Lukic will again miss out for Ipswich against Nottingham Forest.
facts.meaning: Ipswich lose their most-used midfielder this season (7 apps, 1 assist, 6.7 rating) for a game where the middle of the park matters.

facts.fact: Nottingham Forest are rated 42.5% to win at Ipswich, against Ipswich's 29.7%.
facts.meaning: The market still makes the 19th-placed side clear favourites away from home.

facts.fact: Forest have averaged 1.72 xG across their last five league games but scored only 3 goals in that run.
facts.meaning: They are generating chances without converting them — the gap between xG and goals is the story of their false start.

facts.fact: Oliver Glasner has confirmed Morgan Gibbs-White is fit to return at Ipswich after missing the Arsenal defeat.
facts.meaning: Forest's highest-rated player (6 apps, 1 goal, 2 assists this season) is back for the game they most need to win.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line sits at +0.24 in Ipswich's favour — Forest are rated only about a quarter of a goal better.
facts.meaning: Despite being clear favourites, Forest are not seen as a side that wins comfortably; the market expects a tight game.

facts.fact: The goals fair line is 2.7, with Over 2.75 priced at 48.8%.
facts.meaning: The market expects a game just under three goals — closer to a 2-1 than a 1-0 or a 3-2.

facts.fact: The Guardian reports that Forest's false start has placed early focus on Oliver Glasner, questioning whether his tactics fit the squad.
facts.meaning: Friday night at Ipswich is a pressure game for a coach whose side have won once in the league this season.

sources.fact: Oliver Glasner has confirmed Morgan Gibbs-White is fit to return for Nottingham Forest at Ipswich after missing the weekend defeat to Arsenal.
The Athletic reports that defender Nikola Milenkovic should also be fit for Friday's Premier League game at Portman Road.
Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil has confirmed midfielder Sasa Lukic will again miss out against Nottingham Forest.
Nottingham Forest lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal on Sunday, October 18, 2026, and sit in the bottom three ahead of the trip to Ipswich.
The Guardian reports that Forest's false start has placed early focus on Oliver Glasner, with his tactics needing adapting to and the owner not the patient type.
Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner is feeling the heat from some supporters after a drab start at the City Ground, according to Nottingham Forest News.
Ipswich fan Lucas said on BBC Radio Suffolk that the switch to three centre-backs alongside two full-backs gave the team a lot of stability in Saturday's narrow 3-2 defeat at Manchester City.
Bloomberg reports that Clara Vista Investment Partners, one of Ipswich Town's main backers, is seeking to raise $250 million to invest in more football teams.
